title: Where to Buy American Gold Eagles: How to Compare Premiums
summary: Buying American Gold Eagles? Compare online dealers, local coin shops, and marketplaces on premium over spot, fees, and the bid you could sell back into.
body_markdown:
You can't buy a bullion Gold Eagle from the US Mint. The Mint[doesn't sell its bullion coins to the public at all](https://www.usmint.gov/coin-programs/bullion-coins/) : it sells them in bulk to a short list of authorized purchasers. Every bullion Eagle you'll ever see for sale started there and reached its seller by way of a dealer, a coin shop or somebody reselling one they already owned. So asking for the best place to buy gold eagles gets you a narrower answer than a store name. It's whoever has the lowest total cost on the exact version you want at the moment you buy (a[1 oz Gold Eagle](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/american-gold-eagle-1oz-bu-varied-year000207) with a random date is one product; a proof is a different one). Line up each seller's price for one version as a premium over spot and add what paying and shipping cost. Then compare.


Pure runs one of the options below (a marketplace), so read that part knowing we have a stake in it. The math works at every seller.


## Which Gold Eagle You're Pricing Sets the Premium


"Gold Eagle" covers several products that don't price alike, even though the gold in each size never changes. The law that created the coin fixes the 1 oz at[33.931 grams total with one troy ounce of fine gold inside](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title31/html/USCODE-2023-title31-subtitleIV-chap51-subchapII-sec5112.htm) ; what moves the price is everything else about it.


### Bullion Eagles, Current Year or Random Year


The coin most people mean. Dealers usually list it twice: once as the current year, once as "random year," where the seller picks which date you get. Some buyers want the newest date, so the current-year coin can cost more. On Pure at 5:43 PM Pacific on November 23, 2026, the related-listings row showed the random-date 1 oz at 3.98% over spot and the[2026 1 oz Eagle](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/2026-american-gold-eagle-1-oz-50-coin0161) at 8.33%.


### Proof and Burnished Eagles From the US Mint


These are collector strikes. The Mint sells them itself, through its[online shop](https://www.usmint.gov/coins/coin-programs/american-eagle-coins/shop-gold/) . If all you want is the gold, skip them. A proof holds the gold its size calls for; the extra you pay is for the finish and the case. If you want one anyway, Pure lists[proof Gold Eagles](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/1-oz-proof-american-gold-eagle-ngc-random-year000164) too, NGC-graded ones included.


### Why Fractional Eagles Carry a Bigger Premium per Ounce


The markup on small coins starts at the Mint, which charges its authorized purchasers[a 3% premium on the 1 oz Gold Eagle, stepping up to 9% on the tenth-ounce](https://www.coinworld.com/news/precious-metals/mint-s-authorized-purchasers-assess-needs-for-2026) (5% on the half, 7% on the quarter). Every reseller's margin goes on top.


Pure's listings showed it too. Around 5:47 PM Pacific on November 23, 2026, within half a minute of each other, the random-date pages showed lowest asks of 9.56% over spot on the[1/10 oz](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/110th-oz-american-gold-eagle-random-date000002) , 8.00% for the[quarter-ounce](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/14-oz-american-gold-eagle-25-coin-random-date000004) , 4.53% for the[half](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/12-oz-american-gold-eagle-25-gold-coin-random-date000006) and 4.00% for a full ounce. A tenth-ounce still makes a nice gift; you're paying for the size, that's all.

## The Places That Sell American Gold Eagles


### Online Bullion Dealers


The biggest category. Also the simplest. A dealer posts one price per product and ships from its own stock. Many quote a lower price for a bank wire or ACH than for a card; look at both numbers before you compare against anyone else, because shipping and insurance get added at checkout as well (some dealers drop shipping over a certain order size). People stick with a dealer they trust for good reason, since an established one has its reputation riding on every coin it sends out and a track record you can look up before you order.


### Local Coin Shops


You hold the coin before paying and walk out with it. No shipping. The catch is seeing one shop's price at a time, since a second quote means a second drive. Ask the price per coin and whether card costs more than cash. Then ask what they'd pay you for that coin today; a counter that handles Eagles every day answers without blinking.


### The US Mint, for Collector Versions Only


Covered above. Proofs and burnished coins, yes; bullion, no.


### Auction Sites and Private Sellers


Prices range widely here, in both directions. Fees and return terms differ by listing and by platform, so read all of it. Authentication is mostly on you here, so check the seller's history and the return terms before you bid.


### Marketplaces Where Sellers Set Their Own Prices


[That's how Pure works](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-the-pure-marketplace-works) . Many sellers can list the same Eagle, each at their own asking price, while buyers post bids. The lowest ask sits on top. Take it and the order fills right away, or post a bid at your own number and wait for a seller to come to it. Prices are public. You don't need an account to look.


Nothing ships straight from a seller to you: the coin comes to us first, a person checks it in house against the listing, then it goes out insured (shipments are covered both ways, up to $125,000). Keep a dealer you like and use Pure too; looking up the Pure price before you buy anywhere costs nothing.

## How to Compare Gold Eagle Prices Across Sellers


### Turn Every Price Into a Premium Over Spot


Spot is the live price of one troy ounce of gold ([more on spot](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-does-spot-price-mean) ). Because a 1 oz Eagle holds exactly one ounce, its premium is simply the price minus spot. Made-up round numbers to show it: if spot were $3,000, a seller asking $3,120 would be $120 over, or 4%. For a tenth-ounce coin, subtract a tenth of spot.


Take spot from one place ([Pure's gold chart](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/gold) works) at the moment you compare. Gold moves all day. A quote from 9 AM and another from 3 PM can look far apart with identical premiums.


### Add Payment Fees, Shipping, and Insurance Before You Compare


Checkout changes the math. Put card surcharges, flat shipping and any separate insurance charge on top of the coin price, then work the premium out again (our[guide to comparing gold premiums and fees](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/best-place-to-buy-gold-online) covers each add-on that shows up after the listing price).


### Look at the Bid as Well as the Ask


The ask is the price a seller will let the coin go for right now. The bid is the most a buyer will pay for it right now, which is what selling the coin would fetch at that moment (nothing more; it says nothing about where prices go next). Between them sits the cost of buying and turning straight around to sell.


Dealers usually show one number. Ask what they'd pay for that coin and you've got their bid as well.


## A 1 oz Gold Eagle Listing on Pure, as of November 23, 2026


*The 1 oz random-date Gold Eagle listing on Pure, captured November 23, 2026 at 5:44 PM Pacific. Prices move with spot; the live page shows the current ones.*


At 5:44 PM Pacific on November 23, the Orderbook tab on Pure's[1 oz random-date Eagle](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/american-gold-eagle-1oz-bu-varied-year000207) listed four asks and four bids. Lowest ask: $3,820.53, which the page showed as 3.98% over spot. Highest bid: $3,782.78 (3.04%).


Further up the ask side, sellers wanted $3,872.56, $3,919.23 and $4,475.00; the page put that last one at 21.79% over spot. Same coin, same minute. Bids ran down to $3,744.73 (2.00%). The page counted 5,461 of this coin sold on Pure.


If one page can hold asks that far apart for an identical coin, two websites can too, which is the whole case for checking before you pay.


## Checking That the Gold Eagle You Receive Is Genuine


Start with the specs. A real 1 oz Eagle weighs 33.931 grams and measures 32.7 mm across, so a jeweler's scale and calipers will catch a crude fake. A good fake can pass both. That's why the seller's process counts for more than your kitchen tools; our[guide to telling if gold is real](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-gold-is-real) covers the home tests and where each one runs out.


Dealers and shops check what they buy in. On Pure the check happens in house on every item before it ships; coins that clear it carry the Pure Qualified label.


## Choosing Between a Gold Eagle and a Maple Leaf


Both hold one troy ounce of gold. They differ in purity and alloy. Each mint also fights counterfeits its own way. If you haven't settled on the Eagle, our[Gold Maple Leaf vs American Gold Eagle](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/gold-maple-leaf-vs-american-gold-eagle) comparison puts the specs side by side.


## Gold Eagle Buying Questions


### Can You Buy Gold Eagles Directly From the US Mint?


Proof and burnished versions, yes. Bullion, no: the Mint sells it only to authorized purchasers, by law at[the market value of the gold plus the cost of minting, marketing and distributing it](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title31/html/USCODE-2023-title31-subtitleIV-chap51-subchapII-sec5112.htm) . So even the Mint's own first sale is above spot.


### Why Do Sellers Charge Different Prices for the Same Gold Eagle?


Every seller is pricing its own situation. What it paid for the coin, what holding stock and shipping cost it, how it takes payment, how fast it wants to sell. A dealer rolls all of that into one posted price; on a marketplace each seller sets a separate ask, so one coin shows several prices at once and the lowest ask is the one to compare.


### Does a 22-Karat Gold Eagle Hold a Full Ounce of Gold?


Yes. The silver and copper are extra weight on top of a full[troy ounce](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-is-a-troy-ounce) of fine gold, which is why a 1 oz Eagle weighs 33.931 grams instead of 31.1.


### Is a Random-Year Gold Eagle the Same Coin as a Current-Year One?


Gold and size are fixed by statute. The design isn't. Coins from 1986 into 2021 carry the original family-of-eagles reverse.[In mid-2021 the Mint switched](https://www.coinworld.com/news/us-coins/mint-confirms-2021-american-eagle-coins-will-have-old-and-new-designs) to Jennie Norris's eagle-head design (collectors call them Type 1 and Type 2). Order random year and the seller picks the date, so either could show up.
